source_read: PMC HTML, PMC3556483 (author manuscript of Arch Gen Psychiatry 2012;69(7):690-697), read in full in my own browser tab: abstract, Methods (with the 9-register list), Results, Tables 1-6, Figure legend, Comment, Methodological limitations, Conclusions, funding. Inline chi-square values (rendered by MathJax, blank in the page text) read from the page's MathJax source. Figure image not needed (its values come from Table 6).

claims.overstatement: No material overstatement of this source; the claim is careful (association verb, no heritability, interaction confined to the probability scale, adoption-design limits stated). Minor wording points: (1) 'born in Sweden ... adopted within Sweden' is implied by the requirement of register data on a biological parent but not stated in those words; (2) 'a drug-related conviction' is broader than the paper's crime definition (Crime Register codes 5011 and 5012; convictions only for trafficking or possession, or only alcohol-related, were excluded); (3) 'adoptive siblings, who had no genes in common with the adoptee' would be more accurate as 'not biologically related to the adoptee' (biological siblings reared with the adoptee were excluded); (4) the 'about 0.15 percentage points' slope at the lowest biological-risk decile is a point estimate whose interval includes zero (environmental score with the interaction term: 0.0015, -0.0006 to 0.0036).
claims.note: Every Kendler number in the statement and magnitude checks against the source. Editors' calculation recomputed: with deciles coded 0-9 (Figure legend), slope of the environmental index = 0.0015 + 0.0005 x genetic decile = 0.0015 at decile 0 (0.15 percentage points) and 0.0060 at decile 9 (0.6 points): same as the claim. 820/18,115 = 4.53%; binomial 95% CI 4.22-4.83%, matching 4.2-4.8. 'Up to about 3 in 10 after age 5' = 100 - 70.9 = 29.1% (note 12,783/18,115 = 70.6%, slightly different from the paper's 70.9%). Sibling percentages: in Table 3 the proband is the adoptee and the relative is the sibling, so 10.7% vs 6.1% (full), 7.4% vs 5.3% (half) and 6.2% vs 3.2% (adoptive) are the siblings' own rates grouped by whether the adoptee has a record; the claim words them that way correctly. No heritability or variance-component estimate appears anywhere in the paper (the word occurs only in a cited title), so 'the study estimated no heritability percentage' is right. The paper's own Comment (5th paragraph) says its shared-environment finding is at variance with some adult twin studies whose shared-environment effects fade after adolescence, which supports the claim's parenthetical about the adoptive-sibling association.

anchors.extracted: Population: people born 1950-1993 who had been adopted, with register information on both adoptive parents and at least 1 biological parent; adoptions by biological relatives, or by an adoptive parent living with a biological parent, excluded. Age at first cohabitation with adoptive parents (AFCAP) estimated from addresses in 5-yearly censuses, so it is an upper limit of age at adoption. Two cohorts: AFCAP up to 5 years (n = 12,783) and up to 10 years (n = 18,115); results presented for the full 18,115.

Drug abuse (DA) = ICD-8 304, ICD-9 292 and 304, or ICD-10 F10-F19 except F10 (alcohol) and F17 (tobacco) in the hospital discharge, mortality, primary-care or outpatient registers; or Crime Register codes 5011 and 5012 (crimes related to DA; crimes related only to alcohol, or to trafficking in or possession of drugs, excluded); or retrieval from the Prescribed Drug Register of on average more than 4 daily doses for 12 months of hypnotics and sedatives (ATC N05C, N05BA) or opioids (N02A), people with cancer excluded.

anchors.locator: Methods, numbered list of the 9 registers (after the 1st paragraph)
anchors.extracted: Coverage differs by register: hospital discharge 1964-2009; prescribed drugs 2005-2009; mortality 1961-2009; outpatient care 2001-2009; primary care 2001-2007 and only for 1 million patients in Stockholm and middle Sweden; crime 1973-2007. Biological siblings reared with the adoptee were excluded.

820 unique cases of DA in the cohort: hospital discharge 527, crime 313, outpatient 264, prescribed drugs 118, primary care 8; none found only through the mortality register. Agreement between registers (Table 1): odds ratios from 5.6 (prescriptions vs crime) to 118.0 (discharge vs outpatient).

anchors.locator: Results › General description, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Table 2
anchors.extracted: 18,115 adoptees, mean (SD) age at last information 46.2 (8.5) years: DA prevalence 4.5% (95% CI 4.2-4.8) vs 2.9% in all of Sweden for the same birth years; mean AFCAP 4.4 years. By birth decade (1950-59, 1960-69, 1970-79, 1980-93) the national rate was 2.8%-3.1% with no trend, while the adoptees' rate rose 4.1%, 4.6%, 5.0%, 6.5%; birth year controlled thereafter. Table 2 DA rates: biological parents 5.8%, adoptive parents 1.0% (36,230 with information), biological full siblings 6.3%, half siblings 5.4%, adoptive siblings 3.4%, adoptees 4.5%.

anchors.locator: Results › Drug abuse in biological and adoptive relatives of parents and adopted children with DA, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Adoptees with at least 1 biological parent with DA 8.6% vs 4.2% when neither parent had DA (OR 2.09, 95% CI 1.66-2.62; chi-square(1) = 39.4; P < .001); none, 1 or both biological parents with DA 4.2%, 8.2%, 11.9% (chi-square(2) = 44.0; P < .001); biological father 9.9%, mother 8.2%. Biological full and half siblings of adoptees with DA 10.7% and 7.4% vs 6.1% and 5.3% for siblings of adoptees without (OR 1.84, 1.28-2.64, chi-square(1) = 11.0, P < .001; OR 1.41, 1.19-1.67, chi-square(1) = 9.7, P = .001).

Rate in relative when proband has vs does not have DA, % (95% CI): biological parent (any) -> adopted-away offspring 8.6 (7.0-10.4) vs 4.2 (4.0-4.6); father 9.9 (7.2-12.1) vs 4.4 (4.1-4.7); mother 8.2 (6.3-10.5) vs 4.4 (4.1-4.7); adoptive parent (any) -> adoptive offspring 6.8 (3.6-11.6) vs 4.5 (4.2-4.8); adoptee -> biological full sibling 10.7 (7.6-14.5) vs 6.1 (5.6-6.7); -> half sibling 7.4 (6.3-8.5) vs 5.3 (5.1-5.5); -> adoptive sibling 6.2 (4.5-8.1) vs 3.2 (3.0-3.5). For the sibling rows the percentages are the siblings' own rates, grouped by the adoptee's DA status.

anchors.locator: Results › Drug abuse in biological and adoptive relatives of parents and adopted children with DA, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: Adoptees raised by at least 1 adoptive parent with vs without DA: 6.8% vs 4.5%, OR 1.55 (95% CI 0.86-2.80), chi-square(1) = 2.13, P = .15, not significant. Adoptive siblings of adoptees with vs without DA: 6.2% vs 3.2%, OR 1.95 (1.43-2.65), chi-square(1) = 13.9, P < .001.

Adoptive-family predictors adjusted for one another: maternal divorce OR 1.31 (1.03-1.68), parental death 1.37 (1.08-1.73), convictions 1.25 (1.00-1.56), maternal age 0.98 (0.97-0.99), medical hospitalization 1.17 (1.01-1.35), sibling DA 1.76 (1.16-2.67); adoptive parents' DA univariate only, 1.55 (0.86-2.80). Biological relations: parents' DA univariate 2.09 (1.66-2.63), multivariate 1.44 (1.11-1.85).

anchors.locator: Methods › Statistical analysis, 1st paragraph; Results › Predictors of genetic and environmental risk for DA and their interrelationship, 5th paragraph; Table 6; Figure legend
anchors.extracted: Gene x environment interaction tested only on the scale of raw probabilities (identity link, binomial variance), chosen a priori as more appropriate than the logistic scale; the logistic models (Table 5) have no interaction term. Table 6, model with interaction: genetic score 0.0028 (0.0010 to 0.0048), environmental score 0.0015 (-0.0006 to 0.0036), interaction 0.0005 (0.0001 to 0.0008), P < .05; without interaction: genetic 0.0049 (0.0038 to 0.0060), environmental 0.0036 (0.0024 to 0.0048). Both scores are deciles coded 0-9 (Figure legend). Editors' calculation recomputed: environmental slope 0.15 percentage points per decile at genetic decile 0 (interval includes zero) and 0.6 at decile 9.

Intrauterine effects said to be ruled out because adoptees of fathers with DA had a higher rate than adoptees of mothers with DA; no test is given, and the Table 3 intervals overlap: father 9.9 (7.2-12.1) vs mother 8.2 (6.3-10.5).

Register ascertainment may miss people with DA who never came to medical or legal attention and may include people arrested or treated without DA, or treated for chronic pain with high opioid doses; the construct may be broader than DSM-IV drug dependence; a Norwegian survey found 3.4% lifetime DSM-III-R abuse or dependence vs 2.7% detected in all of Sweden (Results give 2.9%).

Selective placement: earlier Swedish adoption studies found a +0.14 correlation in education between biological and adoptive parents; the genetic and environmental indices here correlate +0.11. At least 70.9% of adoptees lived with their adoptive parents by age 5; children were typically moved shortly after birth to a nursery home, often with trial foster placements. Checks: AFCAP negatively associated with DA; no AFCAP x environment interaction (P = .88); pattern unchanged in the AFCAP up-to-5 subsample (n = 12,783).

The authors describe a strong genetic contribution replicating twin studies but give no heritability or variance-component estimate anywhere in the paper. They note their robust shared-environment finding is at variance with some, not all, adult twin studies, and that twin studies of drug use found shared-environment effects in adolescence that largely disappeared in adulthood; DA in adoptive siblings predicted risk more strongly than DA in adoptive parents.

key_findings.note: Known point settled: in Table 3 the proband is the adoptee and the relative is the sibling, so 10.7% vs 6.1% (full) and 7.4% vs 5.3% (half) are the siblings' own rates grouped by the adoptee's DA record. The card words them that way, correctly.

Same reading for adoptive siblings (6.2% vs 3.2% are the adoptive siblings' rates by the adoptee's record), correctly worded. 'Genetically unrelated' is fair: biological siblings reared with the adoptee were excluded.

Editors' calculation recomputed: 0.0015 + 0.0005 x 0 = 0.15 points and 0.0015 + 0.0005 x 9 = 0.6 points per environmental decile; the slope at the lowest genetic decile has an interval including zero (-0.0006 to 0.0036).

reporting_issues.note: Re-found blind: 1.13^9 = 3.00 and 1.10^9 = 2.36 with deciles coded 0-9 (Figure legend).
Re-found blind (2.9% in Results › General description vs 2.7% in Methodological limitations, 1st paragraph).
Re-found blind: CI-implied chi-square about 15.8 (half siblings) and 18.0 (adoptive siblings) vs printed 9.7 and 13.9; chi-square(1) = 9.7 gives P = .0018.
Re-found blind: the father's interval 7.2-12.1 is skewed the wrong way for a proportion near 10%.

Agree it is an inference: with 527 and 264 cases among 18,115 people the log-odds-ratio standard error would be roughly 0.15, far wider than 115.7-120.4 implies; the paper does not name Table 1's population.

risk_of_bias.note: ROBINS-E some concerns overall; domain judgments reasonable for the familial odds ratios. The risk-index and interaction results are weaker, as the reasoning says.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor is defensible because the abstract's Results report the numbers faithfully; it is close to substantial, since the 'genetic' index includes biological parents' education, divorce and maternal age, the abstract's 'more pathogenic' conclusion rests on a probability-scale interaction alone, and the Comment's 'rule out' of intrauterine effects has no test. All of this is already listed in the card's text.

missed: Known point settled: the paper gives no heritability or variance-component estimate anywhere (the word appears only in a cited title); the card's 'No heritability percentage is estimated' and cannot_establish are right.

design_detail says 'drug-related criminal convictions', broader than the outcome definition the card itself gives under outcomes (Crime Register codes 5011 and 5012; convictions only for trafficking or possession, or only alcohol-related, excluded). The claim repeats 'a drug-related conviction'.

'Born in Sweden' (sample.recruitment) and 'domestic Swedish adoptions' (selection_effects) are inferences from the requirement of register data on a biological parent; the paper does not say so in words.

Minor inconsistencies: Table 4 prints the biological parents' univariate OR as 2.09 (1.66-2.63) against 1.66-2.62 in the abstract and Results; 'at least 70.9%' living with adoptive parents by age 5 does not match the age-5 cohort of 12,783 of 18,115 (70.6%).
